# voix

> voix is a documentation studio that migrates product documentation off
> locked proprietary platforms onto open-source stacks the client owns:
> Markdown in Git, Docusaurus, and a CI/CD publishing pipeline. Engagements
> are one-time deliveries ending in handover, not ongoing retainers.

Founded and run by Maria Gilca from Moldova, working with remote teams.
Contact: mariag@voix.md

This file is generated from the built site, so it never drifts from what is
actually published. Everything listed is public and free to quote and cite.

## Start here

- [voix](https://www.voix.md/): voix moves product documentation off locked platforms onto an open-source stack your team owns: audit, restructure, implement, train, hand over.

- [Services](https://www.voix.md/services/): The four services behind a voix documentation migration: consolidation, platform implementation, team enablement and CI/CD publishing.

## Migration handbook

- [The documentation migration handbook](https://www.voix.md/docs/): A vendor-neutral field guide to moving product documentation off a proprietary platform onto Git, Markdown and a static site generator you own.
- [Documentation architecture](https://www.voix.md/docs/architecture/): Define content types, navigation, naming rules and versioning before you move a page, so the structure survives product change.
- [Content types and templates](https://www.voix.md/docs/architecture/content-types-and-templates/): Define a small set of documentation content types, give each a template and a frontmatter contract, and make the structure enforceable.
- [Naming and controlled vocabulary](https://www.voix.md/docs/architecture/naming-and-vocabulary/): Rules for file names, URL slugs, page titles and product terminology, plus how to enforce a controlled vocabulary in CI so terms stop drifting.
- [Navigation models](https://www.voix.md/docs/architecture/navigation-models/): Choose a documentation navigation model - by product, by task, by audience or by lifecycle - and implement it as an explicit sidebar that does not drift.
- [Versioning strategies](https://www.voix.md/docs/architecture/versioning-strategies/): When to version documentation, which model to use - single, snapshot, or branch per release - and what each one costs to maintain over time.
- [Running the migration](https://www.voix.md/docs/migration/): Convert content to clean Markdown, move images and attachments, map every old URL to a new one, and prove the result is correct before you cut over.
- [Converting content to Markdown](https://www.voix.md/docs/migration/converting-to-markdown/): A repeatable pipeline for turning exported HTML into clean Markdown - pandoc settings, post-processing passes, and the MDX pitfalls that break builds.
- [Handling images and attachments](https://www.voix.md/docs/migration/images-and-attachments/): Extract, deduplicate, rename and relocate documentation media during a migration, and choose between colocated assets, static files and Git LFS.
- [QA and link checking](https://www.voix.md/docs/migration/qa-and-link-checking/): The quality gates that prove a migration is correct - automated link and anchor checking, build gates, sampled review, and a launch checklist.
- [Redirect mapping](https://www.voix.md/docs/migration/redirect-mapping/): Build a complete old-to-new URL map, implement it at the right layer, handle anchors and trailing slashes, and verify every redirect before cutover.
- [Operating documentation after launch](https://www.voix.md/docs/operations/): Publishing pipelines, review gates, authoring standards and an ownership model, so the documentation stays accurate after the migration team moves on.
- [Authoring standards](https://www.voix.md/docs/operations/authoring-standards/): A practical house style for product documentation - voice, structure, code samples and links - plus the tooling that makes it the easy path.
- [CI/CD publishing](https://www.voix.md/docs/operations/ci-cd-publishing/): Build and deploy documentation from Git with a pipeline anyone can run - a full workflow, preview deploys, caching and rollback.
- [Ownership and governance](https://www.voix.md/docs/operations/ownership-and-governance/): Assign an owner to every documentation area, set freshness expectations, define how content is archived, and measure whether the docs still work.
- [Review gates and quality checks](https://www.voix.md/docs/operations/review-gates/): Which documentation checks to automate, which to leave to humans, how to configure them, and how to keep required checks fast enough to survive.
- [Planning a documentation migration](https://www.voix.md/docs/planning/): Decide whether a migration is worth doing, inventory what you have, and scope the work before anything moves.
- [Building a content inventory](https://www.voix.md/docs/planning/content-inventory/): How to build a documentation content inventory - crawl the URLs, join analytics, score each page, then decide keep, merge, rewrite or archive.
- [Deciding whether to migrate](https://www.voix.md/docs/planning/deciding-whether-to-migrate/): A decision framework for documentation platform migration - the signals that justify it, the ones that do not, and the full cost of staying put.
- [Scoping and sequencing the work](https://www.voix.md/docs/planning/scoping-and-sequencing/): How to size a documentation migration from inventory data, split it into shippable slices, and order the work so the risky parts fail early and cheaply.
- [Getting stakeholder buy-in](https://www.voix.md/docs/planning/stakeholder-buy-in/): How to win approval for a documentation migration - map who must say yes, write the one-page case, run a pilot, and pre-empt the objections.
